title: Doctors warn of children falling ill with measles and dengue together
excerpt: Dhaka hospitals report at least 10 families with children treated for both in two weeks. Hospitals do not record co-infections separately.
content:
Children in Bangladesh are being treated for measles and dengue at the same time, and doctors say the combination raises the risk of complications, Ajker Patrika reported on Wednesday, 11 November. At least four specialised hospitals in Dhaka said at least 10 families had children treated for both diseases in the past two weeks.

What doctors said

  • Prof Dr Atikul Islam, paediatric infectious disease specialist at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute, said “measles can cause pneumonia and breathing difficulties,” and dengue can make this worse. He said hospitals do not keep separate records of co-infections.
  • Dr F A Asma Khan, superintendent of the Infectious Diseases Hospital in Dhaka, said both diseases have to be treated at the same time.
  • Dr Mirza Golam Sarwar, director of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, said co-infection could raise the risk of complications but such cases are not very common.
  • Epidemiologist Dr Mushtuq Husain said coordinated prevention and control is lacking. Prof Dr Mahmudur Rahman, former director of the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR), noted that the two diseases need different control strategies: vaccination for measles, mosquito control for dengue.

Why it matters

Measles deaths have reached 1,289 this year and dengue deaths 474, and both outbreaks are hitting the same hospitals at once. Without records of co-infection, no one knows how many child deaths involve both. NGOs running child health, nutrition and WASH programmes can combine messages: catch-up measles vaccination, early care for fever, and clearing mosquito breeding sites at home.

Limitations

The co-infection count comes from a small number of Dhaka hospitals and is not systematic. There is no national figure.

Sources

  • Measles and Dengue Co-Infections Raise Health Risks for Children in Bangladesh, Ajker Patrika, 11 November 2026
